verdict.rationale: Homebrew's Bottles docs say that when a formula defines a bottle matching your system, `brew install` downloads and installs it automatically, so no source compile is needed. Casks also install upstream pre-built binaries, and a Trail of Bits auditor independently describes Homebrew as a package manager that "serves its own binary builds." Missing for 10: documentation of where bottles are hosted and cached, of fallback-to-source behavior when no matching bottle exists, and hands-on reports of bottle install speed or reliability.
